<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 270|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIX.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=18|verse=34}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, Saiest thou this of thy self, or haue others told it thee of me? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=35}}† Pilate answered, VVhy, am I a Iewe? {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It pleased God, that Christ who was to dy both for the Iewes & the Gētiles, should be betraied of the one, and put to death by the other.}}∷ Thy nation, and the cheefe priests haue deliuered thee vp to me: vvhat hast thou done? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=36}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, My kingdom is not of this vvorld. if my kingdom vvere of this vvorld, my ministers verily vvould striue that I should not be deliuered to the Ievves. but novv my kingdom is not from hence. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=37}}† Pilate therfore said to him, Art thou a king then? {{sc|Iesvs}} answered, Thou saiest, that I am a king. For this vvas I borne, and for this came I into the vvorld: that I should giue testimonie to the truth. Euery one that is of the truth, heareth my voice. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=38}}† Pilate saith to him, VVhat is truth?

And vvhen he had said this, he vvent forth againe to the Ievves, and saith to them, I finde no cause in him. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=39}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 15. Mr. 15, 6. Lu. 23, 17.''}}* But you haue a custome that I should release one to you in the Pasche: vvil you therfore that I release vnto you the king of the Ievves? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=40}}† They al therfore cried againe, saying, Not him but Barabbas. And Barabbas vvas a theefe.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIX.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Ievves are not satisfied vvith his scourging and irrision. 8 Pilate hearing them say that he made him self the Sonne of God, is more afraid. 12 Yet, they vrging him with his loialty tovvard Cæsar, and professing that them selues vvil no king but Cæsar, he yeldeth vnto them. 17 And so Christ carying his ovvne Crosse, is crucified betwene two theeues, 19 Pilate vvriting notoriously the onely cause of his death to be, for that he is their king or Christ. 23 His garments be so vsed, euen as the Scriptures foretold. 25 He hath special care of his mother to the end. 28 He signifieth al that vvas vvritten of his Passion, to be fulfilled, and so yeldeth vp his ghost. 31 Then by the Ievves meanes also other Scriptures about his legges and side, are fulfilled. 38 And finally, he is honorably buried.''}} {{dropinitial|T|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial T, a bird and a human head.png|imgsize=150px|fl={{verse|chapter=19|verse=1}}}}HEN therfore Pilate tooke {{sc|Iesvs}}, and scourged him.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 27, 27. Mr. 15, 16.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=2}}† And the souldiars platting a crowne of thornes, put it vpon his head: and they put about him a purple garment. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=3}}† And they came to him, and said, Haile king of the Ievves, and they gaue him blovves. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=4}}† Pilate vvent forth againe, and saith to them, Behold I bring him forth vnto you, that you may know that I finde no cause in him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=5}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore vvent forth carying the crovvne of thornes, and the purple vestiment. And he saith to them, Loe the man. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=6}}† Vvhen the cheefe priests therfore and the ministers had seen him,<noinclude>{{rh|||they}}</noinclude>
